full_title: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005

sections.text: This Act may be called the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. It extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir. It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.
sections.chapter: I — Preliminary

sections.text: In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires: (a) 'aggrieved person' means any woman who is, or has been, in a domestic relationship with the respondent and who alleges to have been subjected to any act of domestic violence; (b) 'child' means any person below the age of eighteen years and includes any adopted, step or foster child; (c) 'compensation order' means an order granted under section 22; (d) 'custody order' means an order granted under section 21; (e) 'domestic relationship' means a relationship between two persons who live or have, at any point of time, lived together in a shared household, when they are related by consanguinity, marriage, or through a relationship in the nature of marriage, adoption or are family members living together as a joint family; (f) 'domestic violence' has the meaning assigned to it in section 3; (g) 'dowry' shall have the same meaning as in the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961; (h) 'Magistrate' means the Judicial Magistrate of the first class, or the Metropolitan Magistrate, exercising jurisdiction in the area where the aggrieved person resides temporarily or otherwise or the respondent resides or the domestic violence is alleged to have taken place; (i) 'medical facility' means such facility as may be notified by the Government to be a medical facility for the purposes of this Act; (j) 'monetary relief' means the relief obtainable under section 20; (k) 'notification' means a notification published in the Official Gazette; (l) 'prescribed' means prescribed by rules made under this Act; (m) 'Protection Officer' means an officer appointed under section 8; (n) 'protection order' means an order granted under section 18; (o) 'residence order' means an order granted under section 19; (p) 'respondent' means any adult male person who is, or has been, in a domestic relationship with the aggrieved person and against whom the aggrieved person has sought any relief under this Act: Provided that an aggrieved wife or female living in a relationship in the nature of marriage may also file a complaint against a relative of the respondent or the husband; (q) 'service provider' means an entity registered under section 10; (r) 'shared household' means a household where the aggrieved person lives or has lived in a domestic relationship either singly or along with the respondent and includes such household owned or tenanted by either party or jointly by them, or a household which belongs to a joint family of which the respondent is a member, irrespective of whether the respondent or the aggrieved person has any right, title or interest in the household; (s) 'shelter home' means any shelter home as may be notified by the Government to be a shelter home for the purposes of this Act.
sections.chapter: I — Preliminary

sections.text: For the purposes of this Act, any act, omission or commission or conduct of the respondent shall constitute domestic violence in case it: (a) harms or injures or endangers the health, safety, life, limb or well-being, whether mental or physical, of the aggrieved person or tends to do so and includes causing physical abuse, sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse and economic abuse; or (b) harasses, harms, injures or endangers the aggrieved person with a view to coerce her or any other person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any dowry or other property or valuable security; or (c) has the effect of threatening the aggrieved person or any person related to her by any conduct mentioned in (a) or (b); or (d) otherwise injures or causes harm, whether physical or mental, to the aggrieved person. Explanation I — 'Physical abuse' means any act or conduct which is of such a nature as to cause bodily pain, harm, or danger to life, limb, or health, or impairs the health or development of the aggrieved person, and includes assault, criminal force, and causing hurt. Explanation II — 'Sexual abuse' means any conduct of a sexual nature that abuses, humiliates, degrades, or otherwise violates the dignity of the aggrieved person, and includes any unwelcome act of sexual nature such as forced sexual intercourse, forced watching of pornography, or forcing the aggrieved person to engage in any sexual act against her will. Explanation III — 'Verbal and emotional abuse' includes any insult, ridicule, humiliation, name-calling, repeated threats to cause physical pain, or any other verbal or non-verbal communication that undermines the aggrieved person's self-worth or emotional well-being. Explanation IV — 'Economic abuse' includes deprivation of all or any economic or financial resources to which the aggrieved person is entitled under any law or custom or under any contract or agreement, or which she requires out of necessity; prohibition or restriction of continued access to such resources; and disposal of household effects, alienation of assets, or operation of bank accounts or other property in which the aggrieved person has an interest.
sections.chapter: II — Domestic Violence

sections.section_title: Information to Protection Officer and exclusion of liability
sections.text: Any person who has reason to believe that an act of domestic violence has been or is being committed may give information about it to the Protection Officer. No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against any person for giving information in good faith under this section.
sections.chapter: III — Powers and Duties of Protection Officers, Service Providers, etc.

sections.section_title: Duties of police officers, service providers and Magistrate
sections.text: A police officer, Protection Officer, service provider or Magistrate who has received a complaint of domestic violence or is otherwise present at the scene of an incident of domestic violence shall: (a) inform the aggrieved person of her right to make an application for obtaining relief by way of a protection order, residence order, monetary relief, custody order or compensation order; (b) inform the aggrieved person of the availability of services of service providers and Protection Officers; (c) inform the aggrieved person of her right to free legal services under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987; (d) inform the aggrieved person of her right to file a complaint under section 498A of the Indian Penal Code; and (e) guide the aggrieved person to a shelter home or a medical facility if she so requires.
sections.chapter: III — Powers and Duties of Protection Officers, Service Providers, etc.

sections.text: If an aggrieved person or on her behalf a Protection Officer or a service provider requests the person in charge of a shelter home to provide shelter to her, such person in charge shall provide shelter to the aggrieved person in the shelter home.
sections.chapter: III — Powers and Duties of Protection Officers, Service Providers, etc.

sections.text: If an aggrieved person or, on her behalf, a Protection Officer or a service provider requests the person in charge of a medical facility to provide any medical aid to her, such person in charge shall provide medical aid to the aggrieved person in the medical facility.
sections.chapter: III — Powers and Duties of Protection Officers, Service Providers, etc.

sections.text: The State Government shall, by notification, appoint such number of Protection Officers in each district as it may consider necessary. The Protection Officers shall be under the control and supervision of the Magistrate. The State Government shall also prescribe the qualifications, experience and other conditions of service of Protection Officers.
sections.chapter: III — Powers and Duties of Protection Officers, Service Providers, etc.

sections.section_title: Duties and functions of Protection Officers
sections.text: The Protection Officer shall: (a) assist the Magistrate in the discharge of his functions under this Act; (b) make a domestic incident report to the Magistrate in the prescribed form upon receipt of a complaint of domestic violence; (c) make an application in the prescribed form for an order for monetary relief if the aggrieved person so desires; (d) perform such other duties as may be prescribed by the Central Government or the State Government. The Protection Officer shall be considered a public servant and shall be bound by confidentiality regarding all matters relating to the aggrieved person and the respondent.
sections.chapter: III — Powers and Duties of Protection Officers, Service Providers, etc.

sections.text: Any voluntary association registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 or the Companies Act, 1956 or any other law for the time being in force, having experience in working in the area of social welfare or women's welfare, may register itself as a service provider. A service provider shall have the power to: (a) record any domestic incident report in the prescribed form; (b) get the aggrieved person medically examined; (c) ensure that the aggrieved person is provided shelter in a shelter home, if she so requires. No suit or other legal proceeding shall lie against any service provider or its member or employee for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under this Act.
sections.chapter: III — Powers and Duties of Protection Officers, Service Providers, etc.

sections.text: The Central Government and every State Government shall take all measures to ensure that: (a) the provisions of this Act are given wide publicity through public media; (b) the officers of the Central and State Governments receive periodic sensitization and awareness training on the issues addressed by this Act; (c) effective coordination between ministries, departments and authorities concerning the implementation of this Act; and (d) protocols for various services under this Act including shelter, medical facilities, and legal aid are formulated and circulated.
sections.chapter: III — Powers and Duties of Protection Officers, Service Providers, etc.

sections.text: An aggrieved person or a Protection Officer or any other person on behalf of the aggrieved person may present an application to the Magistrate seeking one or more reliefs under this Act. Every application shall be in the prescribed form and shall contain the particulars of the domestic violence, the nature of relief sought, and such other matters as may be prescribed. The application shall be filed in such manner as may be prescribed. The Magistrate shall fix the first date of hearing, which shall not ordinarily be beyond three days from the date of receipt of the application.
sections.chapter: IV — Procedure for Obtaining Orders of Relief

sections.text: A notice of the date of hearing fixed under section 12 shall be given by the Magistrate to the Protection Officer, who shall get the notice served on the respondent, and on any other person as directed by the Magistrate, within a period of two days or such other reasonable period as may be prescribed. The Protection Officer shall file a declaration of service of notice with the Magistrate.
sections.chapter: IV — Procedure for Obtaining Orders of Relief

sections.text: The Magistrate may, at any stage of the proceedings, direct the respondent or the aggrieved person, either singly or jointly, to undergo counseling with any member of a service provider who possesses such qualifications and experience as may be prescribed. However, the Magistrate shall not refuse to pass any order under this Act merely on the ground that the parties have not undergone or are undergoing counseling.
sections.chapter: IV — Procedure for Obtaining Orders of Relief

sections.text: In any proceedings under this Act, the Magistrate may secure the services of such person, preferably a woman, whether related to the aggrieved person or not, including a person engaged in the promotion of family welfare, as he thinks fit, for the purpose of assisting him in discharging his functions.
sections.chapter: IV — Procedure for Obtaining Orders of Relief

sections.section_title: Proceedings to be held in camera
sections.text: If the Magistrate considers that the circumstances of the case so warrant, and if either party to the proceedings so desires, the Magistrate may conduct the proceedings in camera.
sections.chapter: IV — Procedure for Obtaining Orders of Relief

sections.section_title: Right to reside in a shared household
sections.text: Every woman in a domestic relationship shall have the right to reside in the shared household, whether or not she has any right, title or beneficial interest in the same. The respondent shall not evict or exclude the aggrieved person from the shared household or any part of it except in accordance with the procedure established by law.
sections.chapter: IV — Procedure for Obtaining Orders of Relief

sections.text: The Magistrate may, after giving the aggrieved person and the respondent an opportunity of being heard and on being prima facie satisfied that domestic violence has taken place or is likely to take place, pass a protection order in favour of the aggrieved person prohibiting the respondent from: (a) committing any act of domestic violence; (b) aiding or abetting the commission of domestic violence; (c) entering the place of employment of the aggrieved person or, if the person aggrieved is a child, its school or any other place frequented by the aggrieved person; (d) attempting to communicate in any form with the aggrieved person, including personal, oral or written or electronic or telephonic contact; (e) alienating any assets, operating bank accounts or lockers used or held or enjoyed by both the parties, jointly or singly by the respondent, including her stridhan or any other property held jointly or separately by the parties; (f) causing violence to the aggrieved person's relatives or others who provide her assistance; (g) such other acts as may be prescribed.
sections.chapter: IV — Procedure for Obtaining Orders of Relief

sections.text: The Magistrate may, on being satisfied that domestic violence has taken place, pass a residence order: (a) restraining the respondent from dispossessing or threatening to dispossess the aggrieved person from the shared household; (b) directing the respondent to remove himself from the shared household; (c) restraining the respondent or any of his relatives from entering any portion of the shared household in which the aggrieved person resides; (d) restraining the respondent from alienating or disposing of the shared household or encumbering it; (e) restraining the respondent from renouncing his rights in the shared household except with the leave of the Magistrate; (f) directing the respondent to secure the same level of alternate accommodation for the aggrieved person as enjoyed by her in the shared household, or to pay rent for such alternate accommodation, if the Magistrate considers necessary. The Magistrate may impose any additional conditions or pass any other direction as may be deemed necessary to protect the safety of the aggrieved person or her child.
sections.chapter: IV — Procedure for Obtaining Orders of Relief

sections.text: The Magistrate may direct the respondent to pay monetary relief to meet the expenses incurred and losses suffered by the aggrieved person and any child of the aggrieved person as a result of the domestic violence, including: (a) loss of earnings; (b) medical expenses; (c) loss caused due to the destruction, damage or removal of any property from the control of the aggrieved person; (d) maintenance for the aggrieved person and her children, which shall be in addition to any maintenance payable under any other law; (e) any other reasonable expense. The monetary relief shall be adequate, fair, reasonable and consistent with the standard of living to which the aggrieved person is accustomed. The Magistrate shall have the power to order an appropriate lump sum payment or monthly payments of maintenance. The respondent shall make payment directly to the aggrieved person or through the Protection Officer. Upon failure of the respondent to make payment, the Magistrate may recover the amount as a fine or levy the amount as arrears of land revenue.
sections.chapter: IV — Procedure for Obtaining Orders of Relief

sections.text: The Magistrate may, at any stage of the proceedings, grant temporary custody of any child or children to the aggrieved person or the person making an application on her behalf, and specify the arrangements for visit of such child or children by the respondent. However, the Magistrate shall not refuse to grant such temporary custody merely on the ground that legal proceedings for custody are pending before any other civil or criminal court.
sections.chapter: IV — Procedure for Obtaining Orders of Relief

sections.text: The Magistrate may pass an order directing the respondent to pay compensation and damages for the injuries, including mental torture and emotional distress, caused by the acts of domestic violence committed by the respondent.
sections.chapter: IV — Procedure for Obtaining Orders of Relief

sections.section_title: Power to grant interim and ex parte orders
sections.text: In any proceeding before him under this Act, the Magistrate may pass such interim order as he deems just and proper. If the Magistrate is satisfied that an application prima facie discloses that the respondent is committing or has committed an act of domestic violence or that there is a likelihood that the respondent may commit an act of domestic violence, he may grant an ex parte order on the basis of the affidavit of the aggrieved person under section 18, section 19, section 20, section 21 or section 22.
sections.chapter: IV — Procedure for Obtaining Orders of Relief

sections.section_title: Court to give copies of order free of cost
sections.text: The Magistrate shall, upon request of the aggrieved person, deliver a copy of the protection order, residence order, monetary relief order, custody order or compensation order passed under this Act, free of cost, to the aggrieved person.
sections.chapter: IV — Procedure for Obtaining Orders of Relief

sections.text: A protection order made under section 18 shall be in force until the aggrieved person applies for its modification or revocation. If the Magistrate finds that the respondent has violated the protection order, he may make an order for the removal of the respondent from the shared household for a specified period. An order under this Act may be altered, modified or revoked by the Magistrate on an application made by either party, if the Magistrate is satisfied that there is a change in the circumstances of either party and it is just and proper to do so.
sections.chapter: IV — Procedure for Obtaining Orders of Relief

sections.section_title: Relief in other suits and legal proceedings
sections.text: Any relief available under sections 18, 19, 20, 21 and 22 may also be sought in any legal proceeding, before a civil court, family court or a criminal court, affecting the aggrieved person and the respondent, whether such proceeding was initiated before or after the commencement of this Act. Any relief obtained under this Act shall be without prejudice to any other relief that may be available to the aggrieved person under any other law.
sections.chapter: IV — Procedure for Obtaining Orders of Relief

sections.text: The court of Judicial Magistrate of the first class or the Metropolitan Magistrate, as the case may be, within the local limits of which: (a) the aggrieved person permanently or temporarily resides or carries on business or is employed; or (b) the respondent resides or carries on business or is employed; or (c) the cause of action has arisen, shall have jurisdiction to entertain an application under this Act.
sections.chapter: IV — Procedure for Obtaining Orders of Relief

sections.text: Save as otherwise provided in this Act, all proceedings under sections 12, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22 and 23 and for the contravention of protection orders under section 31 shall be governed by the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. Nothing in this section shall prevent the Magistrate from laying down his own procedure for disposal of an application under section 12 or under sub-section (2) of section 23.
sections.chapter: IV — Procedure for Obtaining Orders of Relief

sections.text: There shall be an appeal from every order of a Magistrate under this Act to the Court of Session within a period of thirty days from the date on which the order is served on the aggrieved person or the respondent, as the case may be. No appeal shall lie from an interim order.
sections.chapter: IV — Procedure for Obtaining Orders of Relief

sections.section_title: Protection Officers and members of service providers to be public servants
sections.text: Every Protection Officer and every member of a service provider shall be deemed to be a public servant within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.
sections.chapter: V — Miscellaneous

sections.section_title: Penalty for breach of protection order by respondent
sections.text: A breach of a protection order, or of an interim protection order, by the respondent shall be an offence and shall be punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to twenty thousand rupees, or with both. A cognizance of the offence shall be taken only on the complaint of the aggrieved person or any other person authorized by the Magistrate.
sections.chapter: V — Miscellaneous

sections.text: The court may, on the sole testimony of the aggrieved person, convict the respondent of an offence under section 31. No provision of this Act shall be construed as preventing the aggrieved person from filing a complaint under section 31 before the Judicial Magistrate or the Metropolitan Magistrate having jurisdiction.
sections.chapter: V — Miscellaneous

sections.section_title: Penalty for not discharging duty by Protection Officer
sections.text: If any Protection Officer fails or refuses to discharge his duties as required under this Act or the rules made thereunder, and no other penalty is provided for such failure or refusal, he shall be punishable with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to twenty thousand rupees, or with both. No prosecution under this section shall be instituted except with the previous sanction of the State Government.
sections.chapter: V — Miscellaneous

sections.section_title: Cognizance of offences committed by Protection Officers
sections.text: No prosecution or other legal proceeding for an offence committed by a Protection Officer shall be instituted except on a complaint filed by the aggrieved person or with the previous sanction of the State Government or of the authority authorised by it in this behalf.
sections.chapter: V — Miscellaneous

sections.section_title: Protection of action taken in good faith
sections.text: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against the Government, any Protection Officer, or any other person for anything done or intended to be done in good faith under this Act or the rules made thereunder.
sections.chapter: V — Miscellaneous

sections.section_title: Act not in derogation of any other law
sections.text: The provisions of this Act shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of, the provisions of any other law for the time being in force.
sections.chapter: V — Miscellaneous

sections.section_title: Power of Central Government to make rules
sections.text: The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act. Every rule made under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before each House of Parliament for a total period of thirty days. If both Houses agree that the rule should not be made or should be modified, the rule shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, without prejudice to the validity of anything previously done under that rule.
sections.chapter: V — Miscellaneous

versions.description: Amendment extending applicability to all India including Jammu and Kashmir
